name: Calvin Montague
summary: At Deathknell's gate, Calvin Montague preys on newly awakened Forsaken leaving the graveyard, tricking passersby into errands for him.

sections.title: A Grifter by the Gate
sections.body: Calvin Montague waits just beyond Deathknell's gates, where the road leads out into Tirisfal Glades. He tries to talk wandering adventurers into carrying his letters, using false pretenses instead of handling his own correspondence or paying a fair courier's fee. Other prominent undead named Montague manage banking interests in the Undercity. Calvin follows a less reputable path, relying on petty schemes and deception.

sections.title: A Rogue's Scheme
sections.body: Calvin Montague offers travelers a sealed message to carry for him. Those with sharp wits or underworld training can quickly see through his words. Newly risen undead may still be searching for purpose in Tirisfal's bleak ruins, but Calvin's offer shows how scarce trust can be in the service of the Dark Lady.

faq.answer: Calvin Montague is a Forsaken rogue waiting near Deathknell's exit gate in Tirisfal Glades. He tries to cheat newly risen undead into running an unpaid errand for him.

faq.q: What does Calvin want adventurers to do?
faq.answer: Calvin Montague tries to talk passing travelers into carrying a letter for him under false pretenses, hoping to get free courier service through smooth talk.

faq.q: Is Calvin Montague related to the Undercity bankers?
faq.answer: Calvin shares his surname with prominent Undercity bankers Ophelia, Mortimer, William, and Randolph Montague. No family relationship has been confirmed.

faq.q: Where can Calvin Montague be found?
faq.answer: Calvin Montague waits along the road just outside Deathknell's wooden northern gate, where he can intercept adventurers heading into Tirisfal Glades.

angles.text: As a Forsaken rogue, you can recognize Calvin Montague's attempt to manipulate the uninitiated as a cheap hustle by a fellow cutpurse.
As one of the newly risen leaving Deathknell, you may learn early that not all of Sylvanas's subjects seek solidarity.
